title: Success is already decided, and it looks like this.
subtitle: The surah opens by defining winning
then: In Makkah the believers were few and looked like the losing side. The surah opens with a flat statement: {reward}they have succeeded.{/reward} Then it lists, one by one, what such people are like.
now: The LinkedIn post about a promotion. The cousin with the new car at the wedding. Your own quiet sense that you are behind. {idea}This verse resets the scoreboard before you even check it.{/idea}
old: Success is what other people can see on me.
new: Success is a set of qualities Allah names, and I can start on them today.
try: Write down your own definition of a successful life in one line. Compare it with the next ten verses.

title: The first mark of success happens inside the prayer.
subtitle: Khushu: a heart that is present
then: Ibn Abbas explained khushu as {idea}fear joined with calm{/idea}. Ali said it lives in the heart. The tafsir notes it only comes to the one who empties his heart of everything else, and then prayer becomes, as the Prophet ﷺ said, {reward}the joy of his eye{/reward}.
now: You start the prayer and by the second rak'ah you are replying to an email in your head. The phone buzzes on the carpet beside you. {trap}You finish and cannot remember which surah you read.{/trap}
old: Prayer is done once I have gone through the motions.
new: Prayer is a meeting, and the heart is the one who has to show up.
try: Before your next prayer, put the phone in another room and take three slow breaths first.

title: Successful people walk past what is useless.
subtitle: Turning away from laghw
then: The tafsir says laghw is falsehood, sin, and {trap}any word or deed of no benefit{/trap}. It links this to another verse: when they pass by it, {idea}they pass by with dignity{/idea}. Qatadah said what came to them from Allah kept them away from it.
now: The group chat starts mocking someone who left. The video feed that eats an hour before bed. The argument in the comments you have no stake in. {idea}You do not have to win it or condemn it. You can just leave.{/idea}
old: It is harmless, I am only listening.
new: My attention is precious. Walking away from the useless is part of success.
try: Mute one chat or feed today that mostly brings you gossip or noise.

title: They keep purifying their wealth and themselves.
subtitle: Zakah as giving and as self-cleaning
then: This was revealed in Makkah, before the detailed zakah rules came in Madinah. Ibn Kathir says the basic duty of giving was already there, and the word may also mean {idea}purifying the soul{/idea}. He suggests both are meant: {reward}the true believer pays attention to both.{/reward}
now: Payday arrives and every pound already has a job: rent, the car, the subscription. Giving gets whatever is left. {idea}This verse puts giving in the same list as prayer, not in the leftovers.{/idea}
old: I will give once I have enough for myself.
new: Giving is how my wealth and my heart both stay clean.
try: Set up one small automatic donation, even a tiny amount, on your next payday.

title: They guard their private lives like something valuable.
subtitle: Chastity as a mark of success
then: The list moves from prayer and giving to private conduct. The tafsir explains these believers {idea}protect themselves from unlawful acts{/idea} and do not do what Allah has forbidden. It is named as part of success, not a side rule.
now: It is late, you are alone with your phone, and one tap leads to another. Nobody would ever know. {idea}Guarding means deciding ahead of time where the gate is{/idea}, not arguing with yourself at midnight.
old: What I do in private only affects me.
new: My private self is something I guard, and guarding it is part of winning.
try: Pick one setting on your phone that makes the late-night slide harder, and turn it on today.

title: What Allah made lawful carries no blame.
subtitle: The guard has a door, not only a wall
then: Right after the call to guard, the verse makes room. Ibn Kathir says the one who seeks {reward}what Allah made permissible for him is not blamed, and there is no sin on him.{/reward} The guard protects something good; it does not condemn it.
now: Some people grow up hearing only warnings about desire, then carry that shame into marriage. {idea}This verse says plainly: in the lawful place, no blame.{/idea} Faith is not meant to make your home cold.
old: Wanting closeness makes me less religious.
new: Allah set a lawful place for desire and called it blameless.
try: Say one warm, sincere word of appreciation to your spouse today, or pray for your future one.

title: Seeking beyond the line is overstepping.
subtitle: Where the boundary sits
then: The verse closes the gap. Whoever seeks other than what was made lawful, Ibn Kathir explains, is among {trap}the transgressors, meaning aggressors{/trap}. The wording is about seeking: the steps toward, not only the final act.
now: The message to an ex that starts as "just checking in." The flirty reply at work you would not show your spouse. {trap}Each small step is a step of seeking.{/trap} {idea}The line is easier to keep far away than up close.{/idea}
old: As long as nothing happens, I have not crossed anything.
new: Seeking beyond the line already counts as stepping over it.
try: Think of one conversation that drifts toward the line. Close it kindly today.

title: They look after what is trusted to them.
subtitle: Trusts and promises kept
then: The tafsir says when they are trusted with something {reward}they do not betray it, and when they promise they are true{/reward}. It contrasts this with the Prophet's ﷺ words on the hypocrite: {trap}he lies, breaks promises, and betrays trust.{/trap}
now: The friend's secret you were told in confidence. The "I'll call you back" you never did. The company laptop, the shared password, the deadline you agreed to. {idea}Small trusts, all day long.{/idea}
old: A small promise is not really a promise.
new: Every trust, big or small, is part of my faith.
try: Find one promise you have let slide, even a small one, and keep it today.

title: The list starts with prayer and ends with prayer.
subtitle: Guarding prayers on time
then: Ibn Masud asked the Prophet ﷺ which deed Allah loves most. He said: {idea}prayer at its appointed time.{/idea} Ibn Kathir notes that Allah {reward}opens and closes this list with prayer{/reward}, which shows its rank.
now: The meeting runs over, then the commute, then dinner, and Asr is suddenly near Maghrib. {trap}Prayer becomes the thing that fits around the day.{/trap} {idea}This verse asks the day to fit around prayer.{/idea}
old: I will pray when I get a free moment.
new: Prayer on time holds the whole list of good qualities together.
try: Set one prayer-time alarm today and stop what you are doing when it rings.

title: People like this are the heirs.
subtitle: Success described as an inheritance

row.title: it is passed to them
sub: a gift with a family likeness

then: After listing the qualities, Allah says: {reward}these are the heirs.{/reward} Ibn Kathir reports a narration that each person has a place in Paradise and a place in the Fire, and the people of Paradise {idea}inherit the places others left empty{/idea}.
now: You have seen families argue over a will. Who gets the house, who was left out. {idea}This verse speaks of an inheritance nobody fights over{/idea}, given to those who carry the family resemblance of faith.
old: Paradise is a prize for perfect people.
new: Paradise is an inheritance for those who grow these qualities.
try: Choose one quality from verses 2 to 9 and do one act of it before tonight.

title: The inheritance is Firdaws, and it is forever.
subtitle: The highest garden, without an end date
then: The Prophet ﷺ said: when you ask Allah for Paradise, {reward}ask for Firdaws{/reward}, for it is the highest and middle of Paradise, the rivers spring from it, and above it is the Throne of the Most Merciful. The verse adds: {idea}they stay there forever.{/idea}
now: You aim high at work, at school, for your kids' futures. Then in dua you ask for "just a small corner." {idea}The Prophet ﷺ told you to ask for the top.{/idea} Hope big where it matters most.
old: Asking for the highest place sounds arrogant.
new: Asking for Firdaws is what I was taught to do.
try: In your next dua, ask Allah for Al-Firdaws by name.

title: Your story starts with a handful of clay.
subtitle: Adam, made from an extract of earth
then: Ibn Kathir says this refers to Adam, made from clay drawn from dust. The Prophet ﷺ said Allah created Adam {idea}from a handful taken from all the earth{/idea}, so his children came in every color and temperament, {reward}red, white, black and in between{/reward}.
now: Someone at work talks down to the cleaner. Someone online sneers at a skin color or an accent. {idea}Every one of them started from the same handful of earth.{/idea} So did you.
old: Some people are simply made of better stuff.
new: We all come from the same earth, shaped by the same hands.
try: Greet someone today whom people usually overlook, warmly and by name if you can.

title: Before anyone knew you, you were held safe.
subtitle: A drop placed in a secure lodging
then: The pronoun moves from Adam to all humans. The tafsir links this to another verse about a weak drop placed {reward}in a place of safety for a known period{/reward}. The womb is {idea}prepared and equipped{/idea} for it.
now: You scroll past an ultrasound photo a friend shared in the family group. A blur in the dark. {idea}You were once that blur, kept safe with no effort of your own.{/idea}
old: I take care of myself.
new: I was cared for long before I could do anything.
try: Thank your mother today, in person, by call, or in a dua for her.

title: Stage after stage, then a new creation entirely.
subtitle: From a clot to a living, seeing person
then: Ibn Kathir explains each stage, then says the soul is breathed in and it {reward}becomes a new creature that can hear, see, understand and move{/reward}. After describing this care stage by stage, Allah says: {idea}So blessed is Allah, the best of creators.{/idea}
now: A baby in a hospital corridor wrapped in a white blanket, eyes barely open. Everyone goes quiet. {idea}That quiet is the right reaction.{/idea} The verse just gives it a name: blessed is Allah.
old: Birth is ordinary. It happens every day.
new: Every person is a step-by-step miracle that ends in a soul.
try: Look at your own hand for ten seconds today and say: tabarak Allah, the best of creators.

title: After all that care, every one of you will die.
subtitle: The stage nobody skips
then: Right after the wonder of creation, the verse says plainly: {idea}after that, you will die.{/idea} Ibn Kathir says after first being created from nothing, {trap}you will eventually die.{/trap} The same Creator who brought you through each stage brings you through this one.
now: A funeral prayer after Jumu'ah. You stand in the row, then go back to your car and check your messages. {idea}The verse wants that moment to last a little longer.{/idea}
old: Death is far off. I will think about it later.
new: Death is the next stage in a story Allah has written with care.
try: Spend two quiet minutes today thinking about what you would want to have done if today were the last.

title: Then you will be raised again.
subtitle: The creation of the Hereafter
then: Ibn Kathir says you will be {idea}created anew{/idea}, souls returned to bodies, and all creation brought to account. {reward}If deeds are good, they are rewarded{/reward}; if bad, punished. The verse comes right after the stages of the womb as if to say: you saw what He can do.
now: You save drafts, back up photos, keep receipts in case you need them later. {idea}This verse says there is a later where your life will be opened again.{/idea} Everything you do today is being saved.
old: Once I am gone, it is all over.
new: The One who made me from nothing will raise me again, and my deeds will be there.
try: Do one good deed today that only Allah will see, and let it be saved for that Day.

title: Seven heavens above you, and none of you is unnoticed.
subtitle: The vast sky and a Creator who is never unaware
then: After man, Allah turns to the heavens, as He often pairs the two. Ibn Kathir says {idea}no heaven hides from Him another, no sea hides what is in its depths{/idea}. He knows what goes into the earth and what comes out, and {reward}He is with you wherever you are.{/reward}
now: Late at night, the city lights, a feeling that no one really sees what you carry. A huge sky and one small person on a balcony. {idea}The sky is vast, and still you are not missed.{/idea}
old: In a universe this big, nobody notices me.
new: The One who built the heavens is never unaware of me.
try: Step outside tonight, look up for one minute, and tell Allah one thing you have told no one.

title: Rain comes measured, and it could be taken away.
subtitle: Water you never had to earn
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah sends rain {reward}not so much it ruins the land, not so little it fails the crops{/reward}. He lists how it could be taken: no rain, sent to the wasteland, made salty, or sunk too deep to reach. {idea}But by His mercy it falls sweet and settles in the earth.{/idea}
now: You fill a glass from the tap without looking. You run the shower for ten minutes. {trap}A water cut in your area for one day and the whole street is in chaos.{/trap} {idea}Every glass is a gift kept in place.{/idea}
old: Water is a utility I pay a bill for.
new: Water is a measured mercy that could be taken any day.
try: Before your next drink of water, pause and say alhamdulillah slowly.

title: From that water, gardens and the fruit you eat.
subtitle: Dates and grapes, and every region's fruit

row.title: fruit
sub: to look at, wait for, eat

then: Dates and grapes were the gardens the people of the Hijaz knew. Ibn Kathir says {idea}the people of each region have fruits that are Allah's blessing to them{/idea}, for which they can never thank Him enough. You look at its beauty, wait for it to ripen, {reward}then eat.{/reward}
now: The mango in summer, the apples in autumn, the bowl of fruit on the kitchen counter that nobody notices until it goes brown. {idea}Your local fruit is your verse.{/idea}
old: Fruit is just something from the supermarket.
new: The fruit near me is a gift grown from rain Allah sent.
try: Eat one piece of fruit today slowly, and thank Allah for the rain behind it.

title: A tree from Sinai gives oil and food.
subtitle: The olive, from a blessed tree
then: Ibn Kathir says this is the olive tree, from the mountain where {idea}Allah spoke to Musa{/idea}, with olive trees around it. The Prophet ﷺ said: {reward}eat olive oil and apply it, for it comes from a blessed tree.{/reward}
now: The bottle of olive oil next to the stove. Bread dipped in it at breakfast with your family. {idea}The Quran pauses on the thing you reach for without thinking.{/idea}
old: Everyday food has nothing to do with faith.
new: Even my kitchen shelf holds signs of Allah's care.
try: At your next meal, name one ingredient and thank Allah for it by name.

title: In livestock there is a lesson, not only a meal.
subtitle: Milk, meat, wool, and much more

row.title: I bought it, it is mine

then: Ibn Kathir lists the gifts: {reward}milk that comes out pure from between dung and blood, meat, wool and hair, and their backs for riding{/reward}. He cites another verse that ends: {idea}will they not then be grateful?{/idea}
now: Milk in your coffee, a wool jumper in winter, a lamb dish at Eid. {idea}You did not design any of it.{/idea} A lesson is sitting on your plate every day.
old: Animals are just products in a shop.
new: Every animal that serves me is a lesson in gratitude.
try: Before your next meal with meat or milk, say bismillah and a short thank you.

title: On them and on ships, you are carried.
subtitle: Every journey rides on something given
then: The list of signs ends with travel. Ibn Kathir notes animals {reward}carry heavy loads to lands you could not reach except with great trouble{/reward}, and cites: {idea}your Lord is full of kindness, Most Merciful.{/idea} The verse then leads into the story of a ship: Nuh's.
now: The plane lands and people clap. The bus gets you to work on time. The car starts on a cold morning. {idea}You were carried again.{/idea}
old: My travel is just logistics.
new: Every journey I make, I am being carried by what Allah gave.
try: On your next trip, say the travel dua or simply: glory to the One who subjected this for us.

title: Nuh's whole message fits in one line.
subtitle: Worship Allah, you have no god but Him
then: The surah turns from signs in creation to the history of Prophets. Nuh came to {trap}warn his people of the punishment for associating partners with Allah{/trap}. His call was simple: {idea}worship Allah, you have no god but Him. Do you not fear Him?{/idea}
now: You give your fears and hopes to many things: the boss's mood, the bank balance, what people think. {idea}Nuh's question still lands: who do you really fear?{/idea}
old: I believe in Allah, so this message is not for me.
new: Worshipping Allah alone means taking back my heart from everything else I fear.
try: Notice one thing you feared today more than Allah. Hand it to Him in a short dua.

title: He is just a man like you, they said.
subtitle: The chiefs attack the messenger, not the message
then: The leaders did not answer Nuh's call. They attacked him: {trap}he is a human like you, he wants to make himself superior{/trap}. If Allah wanted a messenger He would send angels, and {trap}our forefathers never heard of this{/trap}.
now: Someone younger gives you good advice and you think, who is he to tell me? A colleague points out a mistake and you wonder about her motives. {idea}The question is not who said it, but whether it is true.{/idea}
old: I judge advice by who it comes from.
new: Truth can come through an ordinary person, and I should weigh it as truth.
try: Think of one piece of advice you dismissed because of who gave it. Reconsider it honestly.

title: Call him mad, then wait for him to go away.
subtitle: Labeling and waiting as a way to dodge truth
then: They called Nuh {trap}a man possessed by madness{/trap}. Ibn Kathir explains their plan: {trap}wait until he dies, put up with him until you are rid of him.{/trap} Not one argument against what he said.
now: The reminder you keep scrolling past. The friend who invites you to pray, whom you call "a bit extreme" and wait for them to stop. {idea}Waiting out a reminder does not make it go away.{/idea}
old: If I ignore it long enough, the reminder will stop.
new: Labeling a reminder is not the same as answering it.
try: Pick one reminder you have been waiting out, and take one small step on it today.

title: When they denied him, Nuh turned to his Lord.
subtitle: My Lord, help me
then: After long years of calling and being mocked, Nuh asked Allah: {idea}my Lord, help me, because they have denied me.{/idea} Another verse says he called: {trap}I have been overcome{/trap}, so help me.
now: You tried to do the right thing at work and got laughed at in the meeting. Your family dismissed your choice. {idea}Before you rant in the group chat, there is a shorter prayer: Rabbi unsurni.{/idea}
old: When people reject me, I must fight back or quit.
new: When people reject me, I can tell my Lord plainly and ask Him for help.
try: Next time you feel rejected, say quietly: My Lord, help me. Then wait before replying.

title: Build the ship under Our eyes.
subtitle: The answer to his prayer came as a task
then: Allah answered by telling Nuh to {idea}build a strong ship under His watch and guidance{/idea}, then take two of each kind and his family, except those already decreed, who did not believe. He was told {trap}not to plead for the wrongdoers{/trap}, for the decree was set.
now: You prayed for a way out of debt, and the answer looks like a budget spreadsheet and a second shift. {idea}Sometimes help comes as a task, with Allah watching you build.{/idea}
old: If Allah answers my dua, I should not have to work for it.
new: Often His answer is a task, and He watches over me while I do it.
try: Name one dua you have made and one practical step toward it. Take the step today.

title: Once aboard, the first words are praise.
subtitle: Thanking Allah at the moment of rescue
then: Allah taught Nuh what to say once settled on the ship: {idea}praise be to Allah who saved us from the wrongdoing people.{/idea} Ibn Kathir links this to the verse telling riders to {reward}remember the favor of their Lord{/reward} when they mount.
now: The test results come back clear. The job offer arrives. The car skids and stops just in time. {trap}A breath of relief, and then you are on your phone telling everyone.{/trap} {idea}The first word belongs to Allah.{/idea}
old: When things work out, I move on.
new: When I am saved from something, praise is my first word.
try: The next time something goes right today, say alhamdulillah out loud before telling anyone.

title: Ask Him for a blessed place to land.
subtitle: A dua for the end of every journey

row.title: I just need to get there
let it be blessed
sub: He is best at bringing to land

then: Nuh was taught a dua: {reward}My Lord, let me land at a blessed landing place, You are the best to bring to land.{/reward} Ibn Kathir notes that {idea}Nuh mentioned Allah at the beginning of his journey and at its end{/idea}.
now: Moving to a new city. Starting a new school. Walking into a new job on Monday. {idea}You plan the move, but you can ask for the landing to be blessed.{/idea}
old: As long as I arrive, that is enough.
new: Where I land matters, and I can ask Allah to make it blessed.
try: Before your next new beginning, even a small one, recite: Rabbi anzilni munzalan mubarakan.

title: In that are signs, and testing never stops.
subtitle: The flood as evidence and as a test
then: Ibn Kathir says the saving of the believers and the end of the deniers are {idea}clear proof that the Prophets speak the truth{/idea}. And {trap}We are ever putting people to the test{/trap} means Allah tries His servants by sending Messengers.
now: You hear a story from the Quran at a halaqa and think, what a dramatic time to live. {idea}The verse says the test is not over. It is yours now, in quieter clothes.{/idea}
old: Prophets' stories are about other people long ago.
new: The same test runs through my life, in how I answer the message.
try: Ask yourself honestly today: if I had lived in Nuh's town, which side would my habits put me on?

title: A new generation, the same choice.
subtitle: After Nuh's people, another nation
then: After Nuh's people, Allah raised another nation. Ibn Kathir says {idea}some said it was Ad, as the successors of Nuh's people; others said Thamud{/idea}, because of the shout that seized them. The point is the pattern, not the name.
now: Your grandparents had their tests, your parents had theirs. {idea}You are the new generation now.{/idea} The world looks different, but the choice in front of you is the same one.
old: My generation is different. The old lessons do not fit.
new: Each generation gets the same choice in new clothes.
try: Ask an elder in your family what test of faith they faced when young. Listen fully.

title: A messenger from among them, with the same words.
subtitle: The message repeated word for word
then: Allah sent this nation {idea}a messenger from among themselves{/idea}, with exactly Nuh's words: {idea}worship Allah, you have no god but Him.{/idea} Ibn Kathir says he called them to worship Allah alone, {trap}but they belied him and refused to follow him.{/trap}
now: Sometimes the reminder comes from your own sister, your old classmate, the uncle you grew up with. {trap}Familiar voices are the easiest to ignore.{/trap}
old: I know them too well to take them seriously.
new: The truth often comes from someone close, in words I have heard before.
try: Thank someone close to you who once reminded you of Allah.

title: He eats what you eat, so why listen?
subtitle: Comfortable chiefs dismiss an ordinary messenger
then: The verse names who spoke: {trap}the chiefs who denied the meeting of the Hereafter{/trap}, and whom Allah had {reward}given the luxuries of worldly life{/reward}. Their argument: he eats and drinks like you. Ibn Kathir says they refused a human messenger.
now: The more comfortable life gets, the easier it is to wave away reminders. Full fridge, good salary, holidays booked. {trap}Who needs a warning when everything works?{/trap}
old: Life is going well, so I do not need reminding.
new: Comfort is a gift, and it can quietly make me stop listening.
try: On a good day this week, make a short dua thanking Allah and asking Him to keep your heart soft.

title: Obey a man like you, and you lose, they said.
subtitle: Pride dressed up as caution
then: The chiefs warned their people: {trap}if you obey a human being like yourselves, you will be losers.{/trap} They framed following truth as a loss. The next verses show {idea}who actually lost.{/idea}
now: "If you start praying at work, people will think you're weird." "If you stop drinking, you'll lose your friends." {trap}Loss is the first fear used against good change.{/trap}
old: Following this will cost me too much.
new: The real loss is walking away from the truth to protect my image.
try: Name one good change you avoid because of what others might think. Take its smallest first step.

title: Dust and bones, brought out alive? they mocked.
subtitle: Disbelief in being raised again
then: Ibn Kathir says they {trap}denied the meeting with Allah and the idea of physical resurrection{/trap}. Their mocking question: will we come out alive after becoming dust and bones? The surah had already answered: {idea}you were made from clay the first time.{/idea}
now: You walk through a graveyard on the way to the shops. Old names, worn stones. {idea}The question in this verse is quietly asked in your own mind.{/idea} The first eleven verses are its answer.
old: Bringing the dead back sounds impossible.
new: The One who made me from dust can remake me from dust.
try: Visit a graveyard this week, or pass one slowly, and make a dua for those buried there.

title: Far, so far, they said, pushing the promise away.
subtitle: Calling the Hereafter unlikely
then: They repeated the word twice: {trap}far, far is what you are promised.{/trap} Ibn Kathir explains: {trap}very unlikely{/trap}. Not an argument, just a feeling of distance.
now: You are twenty-five, healthy, busy. The Hereafter feels like something for old people in hospital beds. {idea}Feeling far is not the same as being far.{/idea}
old: The Hereafter is so distant it barely matters now.
new: What feels far may be the closest thing in my future.
try: Read verses 15 and 16 again today and let them feel near.

title: This life is all there is, they insisted.
subtitle: A worldview with no second chapter
then: Their creed in one line: {trap}there is nothing but our life of this world. We die and we live, and we will not be raised.{/trap} This is why the chiefs could enjoy their luxury without fear of account.
now: "You only live once." The ad, the song, the friend's caption under a holiday photo. {idea}It is the same sentence, three thousand years later.{/idea} The question is what it makes you do.
old: I only live once, so grab what I can.
new: I live once here, then return, so I live carefully.
try: Next time you hear "you only live once", finish it in your head: and then I return to Allah.

title: Call him a liar, and the matter feels closed.
subtitle: Rejecting the messenger to avoid the message
then: Ibn Kathir says they accused him of {trap}inventing a lie against Allah in his Message, his warnings, and his promise of resurrection{/trap}. Then the final word: {trap}we will not believe him.{/trap} The door was shut from their side.
now: An imam's lecture goes viral with a clip of his mistake, and suddenly nothing he ever said counts. {idea}Discrediting a person can become a way to escape what they said.{/idea}
old: If I can find a flaw in the speaker, I can ignore the message.
new: Truth stands on its own, even when I dislike who said it.
try: Think of one truth you rejected because of the messenger. Look at it again on its own.

title: The second messenger prays the same prayer as Nuh.
subtitle: My Lord, help me

row.title: I am the first to face this

then: Word for word, the messenger repeats Nuh's dua: {idea}my Lord, help me, because they have denied me.{/idea} Ibn Kathir says he {idea}asked his Lord to help him against his people.{/idea} The story shows the same tools in every age.
now: You feel like the only one in the office keeping your values, the only one in your friend group who prays. {idea}You are using a prayer that Prophets used.{/idea}
old: No one has ever felt as alone as I do here.
new: Prophets felt this and turned to Allah with the same few words.
try: When you next feel alone in doing right, say: Rabbi unsurni, and remember who said it first.

title: In a little while, they will regret it.
subtitle: Regret arrives sooner than people think

row.title: plenty of time to fix it

then: Allah answered at once: {trap}in a little while, they will surely be regretful{/trap}. Ibn Kathir says the regret is {trap}for their opposition and stubborn rejection{/trap}. It came sooner than they imagined.
now: The phone call you kept postponing to a sick relative. The apology you were going to make someday. {idea}A little while passes fast.{/idea} Regret is cheapest to avoid today.
old: I have time. I will sort it out later.
new: A little while is all anyone has. I can act before regret comes.
try: Make the call or send the message you have been putting off, today.

title: Proud chiefs became like debris after a flood.
subtitle: The end of the comfortable deniers
then: Ibn Kathir says {trap}the shout overtook them, as they deserved{/trap}, and they became like the scum left by a flood, of no benefit to anyone. He cites: {idea}We wronged them not, but they were the wrongdoers.{/idea} He adds: let those who hear this beware.
now: Everything you build to feel important, the title, the following, the house, can turn to stubble. {idea}What lasts is what you did with it.{/idea} The warning is for your own heart, today.
old: My status and comfort make me safe.
new: Without faith and good deeds, all of it is stubble after a flood.
try: Look at one thing you are proud of and ask: how can I use it for good this week?

title: Then more generations came, one after another.
subtitle: History as a long line of peoples
then: After two detailed stories, the surah speeds up. Ibn Kathir says these are {idea}nations and peoples{/idea}, created one after another, {idea}successors after predecessors{/idea}.
now: Your phone shows a photo from ten years ago, and half the people in it have moved on, some have passed away. {idea}Generations turn faster than they seem to.{/idea}
old: My generation is the main event.
new: I am one generation in a long line, each given its turn.
try: Make a dua today for the generation before you and the one after you.

title: No nation can rush its end or delay it.
subtitle: Every term is written
then: Ibn Kathir says they are taken {idea}at the time decreed by Allah in His Book, before they were created{/idea}, nation after nation, century after century. No one can push the date forward or back.
now: You plan the five-year career, the mortgage term, the retirement age. {idea}Your own term is written too, and you cannot see the date.{/idea} Plans are fine. Assuming time is not.
old: I can count on having the time I have planned for.
new: My time is set by Allah, so I use what I have well.
try: Do one thing today that you have been saving for when you have more time.

title: Messenger after messenger, and nations became stories.
subtitle: What is left of those who denied
then: Ibn Abbas said the messengers came {idea}following one another in succession{/idea}. Each time, most of the people denied. Allah destroyed them and {trap}made them stories and lessons for mankind{/trap}.
now: Someday you will be a story told at a dinner table: what grandpa was like, how she treated people. {idea}Every life ends up as a story. You are writing yours now.{/idea}
old: What people say about me after I am gone does not matter.
new: My life will become a story, and I choose today what kind.
try: Write one sentence you would want your family to say about you. Do one thing toward it.

title: Musa and Harun came with signs and clear proof.
subtitle: Two brothers sent with authority
then: Allah sent Musa and Harun {idea}with decisive evidence and definitive proof{/idea}. Ibn Kathir notes that the problem was never a lack of signs. Musa was not sent alone: {reward}his brother stood with him.{/reward}
now: You keep saying you will change when you are sure, when you have more evidence. {idea}Sometimes the evidence is already enough, and what is missing is the willingness.{/idea}
old: I just need more proof before I commit.
new: The proof is often clear; the real question is my heart.
try: Name one good step you already know is right. Stop waiting for more proof and take it.

title: Pharaoh's court was too proud to listen.
subtitle: Arrogance as the real barrier
then: Ibn Kathir says {trap}Pharaoh and his people were too arrogant to follow them and obey their commands{/trap}, because Musa and Harun were human beings, {idea}just as previous nations had denied{/idea}. Same mentality, different century.
now: Your teenager corrects your grammar. A junior colleague has a better idea in the meeting. {trap}Something in you bristles before you even think.{/trap} {idea}That bristle is where pride lives.{/idea}
old: I am not arrogant; I just know better.
new: Pride can hide inside the feeling that I am above being told.
try: Accept one correction today without defending yourself. Just say thank you.

title: Their people serve us, so why follow them?
subtitle: Looking down on the messenger's people
then: Pharaoh's chiefs said: {trap}should we believe two men like ourselves, while their people serve us in humility?{/trap} The Children of Israel were their laborers. To accept Musa would mean taking guidance from the class they ruled.
now: The cleaner who prays on time. The delivery driver who says bismillah. The refugee neighbor who is more generous than you. {idea}Guidance does not care about the org chart.{/idea}
old: I learn from people above me, not below.
new: Truth can come from anyone, especially those I overlook.
try: Learn one thing today from someone you would normally consider beneath your notice.

title: They denied both brothers and joined the destroyed.
subtitle: The end of Pharaoh's court
then: Ibn Kathir says {trap}Allah destroyed Pharaoh and his chiefs, drowning them all in one day{/trap}. The greatest power of its age joined the list of those who were destroyed, {idea}seized by the All-Mighty, All-Capable{/idea}.
now: Some things in your life feel too big to ever fall: a habit, a fear, a grip someone has on you. {idea}Allah ended an empire in one day.{/idea} He can loosen what holds you.
old: Some powers are just too strong to be changed.
new: No power is permanent before Allah, not even the grip of my own habits.
try: Name one habit you think is too strong to break. Ask Allah for help with it tonight.

title: After the rescue came the Book, so they might be guided.
subtitle: Freedom, then guidance
then: Ibn Kathir says after destroying Pharaoh, Allah gave Musa {idea}the Torah, with rulings, commands and prohibitions{/idea}. He cites another verse: an {reward}enlightenment, guidance and mercy, that they might remember{/reward}.
now: You got through the hard year: the illness, the job loss, the breakup. Now there is space. {idea}What you fill that space with is the next chapter.{/idea}
old: Once the trouble ends, I can relax and drift.
new: After Allah rescues me, it is time to be guided, not to drift.
try: After your next relief, set a small new habit with the Quran, even one verse a day.

title: Maryam and her son became a sign, and Allah sheltered them.
subtitle: A miracle and a safe high ground
then: Ibn Kathir says Isa and Maryam were made {idea}a proof of Allah's ability to do what He wills{/idea}. Then {reward}Allah gave them refuge on high ground with rest and flowing water{/reward}. He says the most apparent meaning is Jerusalem, linking it to the stream under Maryam.
now: A single mother carrying gossip and stares. A family that had to leave home and start again. {idea}The verse names both the trial and the shelter.{/idea} Allah does not raise someone as a sign and then abandon them.
old: If people talk about me, Allah must be against me.
new: Allah can make me a sign and still shelter me through it.
try: Check in today on someone who is carrying people's judgment. Offer them a kind word.

title: Eat what is good, then do good.
subtitle: Lawful food feeds righteous deeds
then: Ibn Kathir says eating lawful food {idea}helps one do righteous deeds{/idea}. The Prophet ﷺ said Allah is good and only accepts what is good, then described a traveller raising his hands, {trap}but his food, drink and clothing are unlawful, so how can he be answered?{/trap} Every Prophet worked; Dawud ate from his own hands.
now: The shortcut at work that bends the truth on an invoice. The extra hour claimed but not worked. {trap}The money buys groceries, and the groceries feed the hands you raise in dua.{/trap}
old: How I earn and how I pray are separate things.
new: What I earn feeds my body, and my body is what I pray with.
try: Look at one source of your income and make sure it is fully honest this week.

title: All the Prophets share one religion and one Lord.
subtitle: One community, one call
then: Ibn Kathir explains: {idea}your religion, O Prophets, is one religion and one group: the call to worship Allah alone with no partner.{/idea} Then: {reward}I am your Lord, so be mindful of Me.{/reward}
now: The family debate about whose masjid is better. The online argument about which teacher is right. {idea}Step back far enough and every Prophet is standing in the same row.{/idea}
old: My little group is the whole of the truth.
new: I belong to one long community of Prophets and believers.
try: Say something kind today about a Muslim who practices a little differently from you.

title: They split into factions, each happy with its own.
subtitle: Division and self-satisfaction
then: Ibn Kathir says the nations to whom Prophets were sent {trap}broke their religion into sects{/trap}, and {trap}each rejoiced in its misguidance because it thought it was rightly guided{/trap}. The comfort itself was the problem.
now: You share a clip that mocks people who think differently, and feel good about it. {trap}That warm feeling of being on the right team{/trap} is exactly what the verse warns about. {idea}The question points at your own heart.{/idea}
old: Feeling sure of my side means I am right.
new: Rejoicing in my side is not proof; sincere checking is.
try: Before sharing anything that mocks another group, pause and ask what it does to your own heart.

title: Leave them in their confusion for a while.
subtitle: A respite that is not approval

row.title: nothing happens, so it is fine

then: Allah tells the Prophet ﷺ to leave them in their error {trap}until the appointed time{/trap}. Ibn Kathir links it to: {idea}let them eat and enjoy and be distracted by hope; they will come to know.{/idea}
now: You know something in your life is off, but nothing bad has happened yet, so you leave it. {idea}Quiet is not the same as approval.{/idea} The respite is a gift to use, not a sign to keep going.
old: If nothing bad has happened, I must be fine.
new: Time without consequence is a chance to turn back, not a green light.
try: Name one thing you keep doing only because nothing has gone wrong yet. Start changing it today.

title: Do they think wealth and children prove Allah loves them?
subtitle: Mistaking gifts for approval
then: Ibn Kathir asks: {trap}do these deceived people think what We give them is because they are honored in Our sight?{/trap} He cites: it is not your wealth nor your children that bring you near to Us, {idea}but only whoever believes and does righteous deeds.{/idea}
now: The pay rise, the new baby, the house with a garden. A voice inside says: Allah must be pleased with me. {idea}Maybe. But the gift is not the proof. What you do with it is.{/idea}
old: Blessings in my life mean Allah is pleased with me.
new: Blessings are a test; faith and deeds are what bring me near.
try: Take one blessing you have and use it for someone else's good today.

title: We hasten good things for them? No, they do not perceive.
subtitle: The world is given to all; faith only to the loved
then: The Prophet ﷺ said: {reward}Allah gives the world to those He loves and those He does not, but gives religion only to those He loves.{/reward} So the verse says: {trap}they do not perceive{/trap} what their wealth really means.
now: You scroll past someone's holiday, car, wedding, and feel left behind. {idea}If you have faith in your heart, you were given the gift Allah gives only to those He loves.{/idea}
old: Others are more blessed because they have more.
new: If I have faith, I already hold the gift that counts most.
try: When you next feel envious online, close the app and thank Allah for your faith by name.

title: The doers of good still live in awe of their Lord.
subtitle: Good deeds paired with humble fear
then: After the warning about those who feel secure in their wealth, the surah describes the opposite. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: {idea}the believer combines excellence with awe{/idea}, {trap}while the disbeliever combines evil deeds with a sense of security{/trap}.
now: You prayed all five today, gave to the fundraiser, called your mother. A small voice says: I am one of the good ones now. {idea}The verse keeps that voice humble.{/idea}
old: Once I am doing good, I can stop worrying.
new: Doing good and staying in awe of Allah go together.
try: After your next good deed, say quietly: O Allah, accept it from me.

title: They believe in the signs of their Lord.
subtitle: Signs in creation and in revelation
then: Ibn Kathir says they believe in {idea}His universal and legislative signs{/idea}, as Maryam testified to {reward}the words of her Lord and His scriptures{/reward}. She accepted that what exists happens by His decree, and what He commands is what He loves.
now: You accept the verses that comfort you and scroll past the ones that ask something hard. You thank Allah for the good news and blame bad luck for the rest. {idea}Belief takes both.{/idea}
old: I believe in the parts that make sense to me.
new: Everything that happens and everything He commands are signs from the same Lord.
try: Read one verse today that you usually skip, and sit with what it asks of you.

title: They give their Lord no partners.
subtitle: Worship kept for Allah alone

row.title: Allah alone
sub: no wife, no offspring, no equal

then: Ibn Kathir says they {idea}worship Him alone and know there is no god but Allah, the One, the Self-Sufficient{/idea}, with none comparable or equal to Him. It comes right after awe and belief, as their foundation.
now: You would never bow to a statue. But the job, the approval of people, the money that you check five times a day. {trap}Partners can sneak in without a shrine.{/trap}
old: Shirk is something only idol-worshippers do.
new: Keeping Allah alone means watching what quietly takes His place in my heart.
try: Ask yourself honestly: what did I think about most today? Give that worry to Allah in dua.

title: They give, and still fear it may not be accepted.
subtitle: Generous hands, humble hearts
then: Aisha asked the Prophet ﷺ if these were people who sin while fearing Allah. He said: {idea}no, daughter of As-Siddiq, they are those who pray, fast and give in charity, fearing it will not be accepted from them.{/idea}
now: You hit donate and a little pride rises: that was generous. {idea}This verse describes a different feeling: hoping it is enough, not sure, still giving.{/idea}
old: Once I have given, my part is done and counted.
new: I give my best and still hope Allah accepts it.
try: Give something small today in secret, then ask Allah to accept it.

title: These are the ones racing to good deeds.
subtitle: The real hastening to good
then: Verse 56 asked whether wealth meant Allah was {trap}hastening good things{/trap} to the heedless. Here the same word turns: the people of awe, belief, and humble giving are {idea}the ones who hasten to good deeds and are foremost in them.{/idea}
now: Someone in the family chat asks for help and you wait to see if anyone else answers first. {idea}The verse describes the one who answers first, without waiting.{/idea}
old: Someone else will step up for that.
new: Being first to do good is the race worth winning.
try: When the next request for help comes today, be the first to respond.

title: No soul is asked beyond what it can carry.
subtitle: Fair burden, a truthful record

row.title: I can never be like them

then: After describing the foremost in good, Allah reassures: {idea}He does not burden any soul with more than it can bear.{/idea} Ibn Kathir says the record omits {reward}none of their good deeds{/reward}, and for His believing servants He will {reward}forgive and overlook many evil ones{/reward}.
now: You read about people who pray all night and give half their salary, and you feel tired just hearing it. You are a parent with a newborn, or working two jobs. {idea}He asks what you can carry, and records every bit of it.{/idea}
old: If I cannot do it all, it is not worth trying.
new: Allah asks within my capacity, and not one good deed is lost.
try: Pick one good deed that truly fits your life right now, and do it today without guilt.

title: Their hearts are covered over, busy with other deeds.
subtitle: Heedlessness that fills the day
then: Ibn Kathir says their hearts were {trap}covered because of negligence and misguidance{/trap} from the Quran, and they had {trap}other deeds they kept doing{/trap}. Ibn Abbas said this meant the evil they were set on.
now: The Quran sits on the shelf in the living room, a little dusty. The TV is on, the phone is on, the to-do list is long. {trap}It is not that you hate it. You are just covered over.{/trap}
old: I would read more Quran if I had time.
new: A heart can get so covered with busyness that it stops hearing.
try: Put the Quran somewhere you will see it first thing tomorrow, and read one page.

title: When punishment seizes the comfortable, they cry out.
subtitle: Loud calls that come too late
then: Ibn Kathir says when Allah's punishment overtakes {trap}those living a happy life of luxury{/trap}, they {trap}scream their calls for help{/trap}. He cites another verse: they cried out {trap}when there was no longer time for escape.{/trap}
now: Some people only remember to pray in the hospital waiting room. {idea}Calling on Allah in a crisis is good. Knowing Him before the crisis is better.{/idea}
old: I will turn to Allah when I really need Him.
new: The time to call on Allah is now, while things are easy.
try: Make one dua of thanks today on an ordinary, easy day.

title: Do not cry out today; no help is coming.
subtitle: A door that closes
then: Ibn Kathir explains: {trap}no one is going to save you from what has happened, whether you scream or stay silent. There is no escape.{/trap} It is a sober picture of a moment when crying out is too late.
now: Right now, today, your dua is heard. Your tawbah is accepted. {reward}The door this verse describes as closed is wide open for you.{/reward} That is the point of hearing it now.
old: I can always repent later.
new: Repentance is open now, and that is a mercy I should not waste.
try: Make sincere tawbah tonight for one specific thing.

title: The verses were read to you, and you turned on your heels.
subtitle: The greatest of their sins
then: Ibn Kathir says this is the {trap}greatest of their sins{/trap}: the verses were recited to them, and {trap}when they were called, they refused and resisted{/trap}. They were not ignorant. They walked away.
now: The khutbah touches exactly your problem and you think, that is for other people. A friend shares a verse and you swipe past. {trap}Turning on your heels can look like a thumb flicking upward.{/trap}
old: Hearing the Quran is enough.
new: Hearing it and turning away is worse than never hearing it.
try: When a verse lands on you today, stop scrolling and read it twice.

title: Proud of the House, they spent nights talking against it.
subtitle: Late-night talk and empty pride
then: Ibn Abbas said the Quraysh {trap}boasted about the Kabah: we are its people who stay up talking at night.{/trap} They did not use it for its purpose, {trap}so in effect they had abandoned it{/trap}. He said late-night chatter became disliked after this verse.
now: You live near the masjid, or come from a religious family, and that feels like a credential. Meanwhile midnight is for the group chat, the gossip, the scrolling. {idea}Being close to something holy is not the same as living by it.{/idea}
old: My background and closeness to religion protect me.
new: Closeness means nothing if I do not live by what I am close to.
try: Close the chats an hour earlier tonight and spend five minutes in dua or Quran.

title: Have they not reflected on the Quran?
subtitle: A gift given to them, unread
then: Ibn Kathir says no Book or warner had come to their forefathers, so they should have {reward}accepted it, given thanks, tried to understand it and acted on it night and day{/reward}. Qatadah said if they had pondered it, {idea}they would have found a deterrent from disobeying Allah{/idea}.
now: You can recite Al-Fatiha in your sleep, but if someone asked what verse five means, you would pause. {idea}The verse is not asking whether you have heard it. It asks whether you have thought about it.{/idea}
old: I know the Quran because I have read it.
new: Knowing the Quran begins when I stop and think about what it says.
try: Pick one short verse you recite daily. Read its meaning today and think about it for two minutes.

title: Did they not know their own Messenger?
subtitle: They knew his honesty since childhood
then: Ibn Kathir asks: {idea}do they not recognize the honesty, trustworthiness and good character with which he grew up among them?{/idea} Even Abu Sufyan, before Islam, when asked by Heraclius, {reward}could only admit he was noble and truthful{/reward}.
now: You know the person who always tells you the truth, even when it is uncomfortable. When they warn you, you still look for reasons to doubt. {idea}Their track record is the evidence.{/idea}
old: I need to judge every claim from scratch.
new: A lifetime of honesty is strong evidence, and I should honor it.
try: Thank someone today whose honesty you have always been able to rely on.

title: He brought the truth, and most of them disliked it.
subtitle: The problem was not madness but aversion
then: Ibn Kathir says the Quraysh {trap}called him mad or said he made it up, but their hearts did not believe that{/trap}. They knew. Allah names the real reason: {trap}most of them are averse to the truth.{/trap}
now: The doctor says cut the sugar. The friend says you were rude. The verse says pray. {trap}Sometimes you call the message unclear because you do not like what it asks.{/trap}
old: I reject this because it does not make sense.
new: Sometimes I reject a truth because I dislike it, not because it is wrong.
try: Name one truth you have been resisting. Admit to yourself that you know it is true.

title: If truth followed their desires, everything would fall apart.
subtitle: Truth does not bend to wants

picture.label: If it worked the other way

then: Ibn Kathir says if Allah had {trap}answered the desires in their hearts and legislated by them, the heavens and earth would be corrupted{/trap}, because human desires are inconsistent. Instead {idea}We brought them their reminder{/idea}, but they turned from it.
now: You want the rules flexible when they cost you and strict when someone else breaks them. Everyone does. {idea}A truth that bent to everyone's wants would hold nothing up.{/idea}
old: The right answer should fit what I want.
new: Truth stays put; I am the one who has to move.
try: Notice one moment today when you wanted a rule to bend for you. Keep it instead.

title: He asked them for nothing; his reward is with his Lord.
subtitle: A messenger without a fee
then: Al-Hasan said kharj means {idea}a reward{/idea}; Qatadah said {idea}payment{/idea}. Ibn Kathir says the Prophet ﷺ asked for no wages for calling them, {reward}hoping only for a great reward from Allah{/reward}, as the man in another surah said: follow those who ask no wages of you.
now: The friend who helps you move house and refuses the pizza money. The teacher who stays late for free. {idea}Help with no price tag is easier to trust.{/idea} And you can be that person too.
old: Good deeds deserve some payback.
new: The best reward comes from Allah, so I can help without asking anything.
try: Do one favor today and refuse any thanks or payment for it.

title: You are inviting them to a straight path.
subtitle: Reassurance for the Prophet ﷺ
then: After all the objections, Allah tells the Prophet ﷺ plainly: {idea}indeed, you invite them to a straight path.{/idea} Whatever they said about him, {reward}what he called to was right{/reward}.
now: You keep showing up to teach your kids prayer, and they roll their eyes. You keep inviting your friend to the halaqa and they keep saying maybe. {idea}If what you call to is straight, keep calling.{/idea}
old: If nobody listens, I must be doing it wrong.
new: The value of inviting to good is in where it leads, not in the response.
try: Gently invite one person to something good this week, with no pressure.

title: Without belief in the Hereafter, people drift off the path.
subtitle: The compass that keeps you straight
then: Right after the straight path comes its opposite: {trap}those who do not believe in the Hereafter are deviating from the path.{/trap} Ibn Kathir says {trap}they have gone astray and deviated.{/trap}
now: When you forget the Day of Return, small compromises start to look fine. One more lie on the timesheet. One more harsh word. {idea}Remembering the end straightens the road.{/idea}
old: I can stay good without thinking about the Hereafter.
new: Remembering that I will return keeps me on the path.
try: Before a tough decision today, ask: how will this look on the Day I return to Allah?

title: Even relief would not have changed them.
subtitle: When mercy meets a stubborn heart
then: The surah was revealed around the famine in Makkah. Ibn Kathir says Allah tells of their stubbornness: {trap}even if He removed the calamity and made them understand the Quran, they still would not follow it{/trap}, but persist, wandering blindly.
now: "Once this hard month is over, I'll start praying properly." Then the month ends, and nothing changes. {idea}Relief does not fix a heart by itself.{/idea}
old: I will change once my situation improves.
new: If my heart is not willing, better times will not change me.
try: Start one good habit today, during the hard time, instead of waiting for it to pass.

title: Hardship came, and still they would not humble themselves.
subtitle: The famine that should have softened them
then: Ibn Abbas reported that Abu Sufyan came to the Prophet ﷺ saying: {trap}we have been reduced to eating camel hair and blood.{/trap} Then this verse came. Ibn Kathir says Allah {idea}tested them with difficulties{/idea}, {trap}but it did not deter them; they did not call on Him.{/trap}
now: The redundancy letter, the diagnosis, the empty bank account. You call friends, search online, lie awake planning. {idea}The verse asks: did you also bow and ask Him?{/idea}
old: Hardship is something to just get through.
new: Hardship is a door back to Allah, if I humble myself.
try: In your current difficulty, make one long, humble sujood today and tell Allah all of it.

title: When the gate of severe punishment opens, hope collapses.
subtitle: Despair that comes too late
then: Ibn Kathir says when Allah's command {trap}comes to them suddenly and they are overtaken by what they were not expecting, they despair of any ease and goodness, and all their hopes disappear.{/trap}
now: You have hope right now. You can still turn, still apologize, still pray. {reward}That hope is a door this verse says will not stay open forever.{/reward} Use it while it is yours.
old: There will always be another chance.
new: Today's hope is a mercy, and I should use it before it closes.
try: Turn one regret into action today: an apology, a prayer made up, a debt repaid.

title: He gave you hearing, sight, and hearts. Little thanks.
subtitle: The tools you use to know anything

row.title: to know Him and draw lessons

then: Ibn Kathir says Allah gave {reward}hearing, sight and understanding through which they come to know things and draw lessons{/reward}, signs of His Oneness. Then: {trap}how little you thank Allah for the blessings He has given you.{/trap}
now: You listen to podcasts for hours and watch videos until your eyes ache. Your mind replays arguments at 2 a.m. {idea}The same ears, eyes and heart were given so you could notice Him.{/idea}
old: My senses are just part of being alive.
new: My hearing, sight and heart are gifts meant to lead me to Allah.
try: Use your eyes for one minute today just to notice something beautiful, and thank Allah for it.

title: He spread you across the earth and will gather you back.
subtitle: Scattered now, gathered later
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah {idea}put people in all parts of the earth, with their different nations, languages and characteristics{/idea}, and on the Day He will gather them all, {reward}none left out, young or old, noble or insignificant{/reward}.
now: Your family is spread over three time zones, a cousin in Canada, a brother in Dubai, a grandmother back home. {idea}Every one of them, and you, will be gathered in one place.{/idea}
old: We are scattered, and that is just how life is.
new: However far apart we live, we will all be gathered before Allah.
try: Send a message today to a relative who lives far away.

title: Life, death, night and day are His. Will you not think?
subtitle: Signs you live inside every day
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah {idea}will bring the scattered bones back to life{/idea}, and by His command night and day follow each other, never departing from that pattern. Then: {idea}do you not have minds that tell you of the Almighty?{/idea}
now: Your alarm goes off at 6, sunrise at 6:40, sunset at 5:15. Your phone even shows it. {idea}You plan your life around an order you did not set.{/idea}
old: Day and night are just the background of life.
new: Every sunrise and sunset is a sign that Allah gives and takes life.
try: Watch the sunset or sunrise today, even through a window, and think for one minute.

title: They only repeated what earlier peoples said.
subtitle: Old objections in new mouths
then: After all those signs, the answer was no new argument. Ibn Kathir says they {trap}were like the disbelievers who came before them{/trap}, repeating the words of earlier nations, the same ones the surah already told of with Nuh and the next generation.
now: A clever video argues that life after death is a myth, and it feels new and bold. {idea}This verse says: it is one of the oldest lines in history.{/idea}
old: Today's doubts are new and more serious.
new: Most doubts are old echoes the Quran has already answered.
try: When a doubt bothers you this week, look for how the Quran already answered it.

title: Dust and bones, raised again? they asked once more.
subtitle: The same doubt, the same answer

row.title: the One who made them first

then: Ibn Kathir says {trap}they thought it very unlikely, after they had disintegrated into nothing{/trap}. He cites the reply from Surah Ya Sin: {idea}He will give them life who created them the first time.{/idea}
now: You hold an old family photo of a great-grandparent you never met. Nothing is left of them but a name. {idea}The One who first made them from nothing can make them again.{/idea}
old: Once someone is dust, they are gone for good.
new: The One who made me the first time can raise me again.
try: Make a dua today for a relative who has passed away, by name.

title: We heard this promise before. Just old legends, they said.
subtitle: Dismissing truth because it is familiar
then: They said: {trap}we were promised this, we and our fathers before; it is only legends of the ancients.{/trap} Ibn Kathir explains they meant it was something {trap}learned from the books and disputes of the ancients{/trap}, and so impossible.
now: You have heard "death can come any time" so many times it no longer means anything. {trap}Familiar truths are the easiest to stop hearing.{/trap}
old: I have heard it all before, so it does not move me.
new: A truth repeated by every Prophet deserves to be heard fresh.
try: Take one reminder you have heard a hundred times and act on it today as if it were new.

title: Whose is the earth and everyone on it?
subtitle: A question with only one honest answer
then: Allah tells the Prophet ﷺ to ask the idolaters, {idea}who owns the earth and all in it?{/idea} Ibn Kathir says they {reward}admitted Allah was Creator and Owner{/reward}, yet still worshipped others they thought would bring them near Him.
now: Your name is on the house deeds, the car log book, the phone contract. {idea}Ask the question honestly: whose is it really?{/idea} The answer changes how you hold it.
old: What I own is mine.
new: All of it belongs to Allah, including me.
try: Look around your room and say: all of this belongs to Allah. Give one thing away this week.

title: They say it is Allah's. Then why not remember?
subtitle: Knowing the answer but not living it
then: Ibn Kathir says they {reward}admitted the earth belongs to Allah alone{/reward}. So the Prophet ﷺ was told to ask: {idea}will you not then remember that none should be worshipped except the Creator and Provider?{/idea}
now: You would answer "Allah" in a quiz without thinking. Then you spend the day as if the rent, the boss, and your own effort run everything. {idea}The answer is in your head; the verse wants it in your day.{/idea}
old: I already know Allah owns everything.
new: Knowing it is the start; remembering it all day is the point.
try: Set one reminder on your phone today that says: it all belongs to Allah.

title: Who is Lord of the seven heavens and the Great Throne?
subtitle: The question rises higher
then: The question moves from the earth to the sky. Ibn Kathir describes {idea}the higher realm with its planets, lights and angels{/idea}, and the Throne as {reward}the highest of all created things, combining height, vastness and splendor{/reward}. Ibn Masud said the Throne's light is from the light of His Face.
now: The bill, the exam, the argument with your sister: they fill the whole screen of your mind. {idea}Zoom out. The One you pray to is Lord of the Great Throne.{/idea}
old: My problems are bigger than anything else.
new: My Lord is the Lord of the Great Throne, and my problem is small to Him.
try: Before you worry about something today, say: Allah is Lord of the Great Throne. Then ask Him.

title: Again they say Allah. Then will you not be mindful?
subtitle: From remembering to fearing
then: The first reply was {idea}will you not remember?{/idea} Now the response grows: {idea}will you not have taqwa?{/idea} Ibn Kathir says: since you admit He is Lord of the heavens and the Throne, {trap}will you not fear His punishment for worshipping others with Him?{/trap}
now: You say "Allah is great" forty times a day in prayer. Then in the office kitchen you laugh along with a joke you know is wrong. {idea}Admitting His greatness should change how you act when He is the only one watching.{/idea}
old: Saying Allah is great is enough.
new: If I truly admit His greatness, I should be mindful of Him.
try: Pick one moment today when you would normally slip, and pause to remember He sees.

title: He protects, and no one can protect against Him.
subtitle: The control of everything is in His hand
then: Ibn Kathir explains that among the Arabs, if a leader gave someone protection, {idea}no one could go against it{/idea}, yet someone could still protect against that leader. {reward}Allah is the greatest Master; none can overturn His ruling.{/reward} The Prophet ﷺ would swear: by the One who turns the hearts.
now: You are scared of a manager who could end your contract, or a person who has power over your family. {idea}They are held by Someone too.{/idea} His protection is the only one nobody can override.
old: I need the right people on my side to be safe.
new: Only Allah's protection cannot be overruled, so I seek it first.
try: When you feel threatened today, say: Hasbiyallah, Allah is enough for me.

title: They say Allah a third time. So how are you fooled?
subtitle: The final question of the three
then: Three questions, three times they answer: Allah. The last reply is sharpest: {trap}how then are you deceived?{/trap} Ibn Kathir: {trap}how can your minds accept worshipping others when you recognize and acknowledge this?{/trap}
now: You know scrolling at midnight wrecks your morning. You know the sale is a trap. You know the grudge hurts you most. {trap}Knowing is not the same as being free.{/trap} Something keeps fooling you.
old: If I know the truth, I am not being fooled.
new: I can know the truth and still be fooled, so I must act on what I know.
try: Name one thing you know is wrong for you but still do. Take one step away from it today.

title: We brought them the truth, and they are lying.
subtitle: Partners with no evidence

row.title: the truth
sub: no god but Allah, with proof

then: Ibn Kathir says the truth is {idea}the declaration that there is no god but Allah, with clear and sound proof{/idea}. They are liars in worshipping others {trap}with no evidence, only following confused forefathers{/trap}: we found our fathers on a way and we follow it.
now: "That's how my family has always done it." A habit at weddings, a belief about luck, a way of treating people. {idea}Ask: is there proof for this, or only tradition?{/idea}
old: If my family always did it, it must be right.
new: I check what I follow against the truth, not only against custom.
try: Pick one family habit and ask yourself honestly whether it has a real basis.

title: If there were other gods, the universe would fall to fighting.
subtitle: The order of the world points to One
then: Ibn Kathir says if there were many gods, {trap}each would control what he created, so there would be no order{/trap}. But {idea}the universe is ordered and cohesive, upper and lower realms connected perfectly{/idea}. Allah has no son and no partner.
now: Two managers giving opposite instructions, and the whole project collapses. You have seen it at work. {idea}The sky has never had that problem.{/idea}
old: The universe just happens to be orderly.
new: The order I see everywhere points to one Lord alone.
try: Look at one ordered thing today, a leaf, your heartbeat, the clock of the sun, and say: subhanallah.

title: He knows the hidden and the seen.
subtitle: Exalted above any partner
then: Ibn Kathir explains: {idea}He knows what is hidden from His creatures and what they see{/idea}. That is why He is {reward}sanctified, glorified and exalted above all that the wrongdoers say{/reward}.
now: The thought you never said out loud. The reason behind the favor you did. The tears in the car before you walked in smiling. {idea}All of it is known to Him.{/idea}
old: People only know what I show them.
new: Allah knows what I show and what I hide, and I can be honest with Him.
try: Tell Allah tonight about one thing you have hidden from everyone.

title: If You show me what they are promised, my Lord.
subtitle: A dua taught for times of trial
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah {idea}commands His Prophet ﷺ to call on Him with this supplication when calamity strikes{/idea}. The Prophet ﷺ also taught: {reward}if You want to test people, take me to You without being put through the trial.{/reward}
now: When things fall apart around you, a company scandal, a family feud, people you warned now facing the result, {trap}it is easy to feel "I told you so."{/trap} {idea}The verse turns you to ask for your own safety instead.{/idea}
old: When wrongdoers face consequences, I should feel vindicated.
new: When trials come, my concern is my own safety with Allah.
try: When you hear of someone's downfall today, ask Allah to protect you from the same.

title: Then do not put me among the wrongdoing people.
subtitle: Even the Prophet ﷺ asked for this

row.title: everyone
sub: the Prophet ﷺ was taught it

then: Ibn Kathir explains the meaning: {idea}if You punish them while I am witnessing, then do not cause me to be one of them.{/idea} The best of creation was taught to ask {reward}not to be counted with the wrongdoers{/reward}.
now: You think of yourself as one of the good ones. Then you notice how easily you slid into the office gossip, the unfair joke, the group that excludes someone. {idea}Nobody is too good for this dua.{/idea}
old: I am not the kind of person who becomes a wrongdoer.
new: I ask Allah every day not to let me slide into wrong.
try: Add this dua to your prayer today: Rabbi fa la taj'alni fil qawmiz-zalimin.

title: We are able to show you what We promised them.
subtitle: Delay is not inability
then: Ibn Kathir says: {idea}if We willed, We could show you the punishment and test We will send upon them.{/idea} Delay was His choice, {reward}not a lack of power{/reward}. The Prophet ﷺ was being comforted.
now: You have watched someone cheat and prosper, lie and get promoted. It feels like nobody is keeping score. {idea}Allah is able. He has not forgotten.{/idea} Your job is your own conduct.
old: If wrong is not punished now, maybe it never will be.
new: Allah is able, and His timing is His, so I leave it with Him.
try: Hand one injustice that eats at you over to Allah in dua, and let it go for today.

title: Push back their evil with what is better.
subtitle: Answering harm with kindness
then: Ibn Kathir calls this {idea}the best way to behave when mixing with people: treat kindly the one who treats you badly, to soften his heart{/idea}. He cites: then the one with enmity becomes {reward}like a close friend{/reward}, and {idea}none is granted it except the patient.{/idea}
now: Your neighbor complains about your bins again, rudely. The colleague takes credit for your work. {idea}The verse asks for a better reply than the one they gave you.{/idea} Allah knows what they said.
old: If they are rude, I am allowed to be rude back.
new: Answering harm with better is harder and stronger.
try: Answer the next rude message you get with a calm, kind reply.

title: Seek refuge from the devils' prodding.
subtitle: Kindness for people, refuge from Shaytan
then: After teaching kindness to people, Allah teaches a different response to Shaytan: {idea}seek refuge, because no trick helps against them and kindness cannot protect you.{/idea} The Prophet ﷺ sought refuge {trap}from his whisperings, evil suggestions and insinuations{/trap}.
now: That sudden urge to snap at your child. The thought that pops up mid-prayer. The voice saying one more episode, skip Fajr. {idea}You do not have to debate it. Seek refuge.{/idea}
old: I can handle bad thoughts on my own.
new: Whispers are beaten by seeking refuge with Allah, not by arguing.
try: The next time a bad urge hits today, say a'udhu billahi minash-shaytanir-rajim before you act.

title: And refuge lest they come near me at all.
subtitle: Starting every act with Allah's name
then: Ibn Kathir says this means {idea}in any issue of my life{/idea}, so we mention Allah at the start of eating, intimacy and slaughter to ward them off. The Prophet ﷺ sought refuge from {trap}being assaulted by Shaytan at the time of death{/trap}.
now: You grab food from the fridge and start eating without a word. You leave the house in a rush. {idea}A whispered bismillah is a closed door.{/idea}
old: Shaytan only matters in big moments.
new: Mentioning Allah at the start of ordinary acts keeps Shaytan away.
try: Say bismillah before every meal and every time you leave the house today.

title: When death comes, he says: my Lord, send me back.
subtitle: The request everyone will understand too late

row.title: acts of obedience
sub: that is all he will want

then: Ibn Kathir says this is when death comes to {trap}the disbeliever or one negligent with Allah's commands{/trap}. Qatadah said he will not wish to return for family or wealth, {idea}only to obey Allah. May Allah have mercy on a man who does now what the disbeliever will wish he had done.{/idea}
now: You are alive right now, reading this. {idea}You already are the person who got sent back.{/idea} Every day you wake up is the thing he begs for.
old: I will get serious about my faith someday.
new: Today is the second chance others will beg for.
try: Do one act of obedience today that you would wish for if you were on your deathbed.

title: No. It is only a word, and a barrier stands behind them.
subtitle: The request refused, then the Barzakh
then: Ibn Kathir says kalla is {trap}a word of rebuke: We will not accept it{/trap}. His request is {trap}just talk, not accompanied by action{/trap}. Then comes the Barzakh, which Mujahid called {idea}a barrier between this world and the Hereafter{/idea}, lasting until the Day of Resurrection.
now: "I'll start next Monday." "After Ramadan." "When the kids are older." {trap}Those are words.{/trap} {idea}The verse says words without deeds are what the dying man offers, and they are refused.{/idea}
old: My good intentions count, even if I have not acted yet.
new: An intention only becomes real when I act on it, while I still can.
try: Turn one "I will someday" into something you do before tonight.

title: When the Horn is blown, family ties will not help.
subtitle: No lineage, no asking after each other
then: Ibn Kathir says {trap}lineage will be of no avail; a father will not ask about his son{/trap}, even if he sees him. Ibn Masud said a voice will call: {idea}whoever is owed something, come and take it{/idea}, and a person will be glad to be owed even a little by his father, child or spouse.
now: "Do you know who my family is?" Or the quiet comfort that your parents are pious, so you will be fine. {idea}On that Day, your own record walks with you.{/idea} So does every small wrong you owe your family.
old: My family's goodness will cover for me.
new: I will stand on my own deeds, so I settle what I owe people now.
try: Settle one small thing you owe a family member today: money, an apology, a promise.

title: Heavy scales mean success.
subtitle: Even one extra good deed can tip it
then: Ibn Abbas said this is {reward}the one whose good deeds outweigh his bad deeds, even by one{/reward}. They are the ones who {reward}attained what they wanted and were saved{/reward}. The surah that opened with "the believers have succeeded" returns to the same word.
now: Smiling at the tired cashier. Picking up the litter outside the masjid. Texting your mum good night. {idea}You will never know which small deed tipped your scale.{/idea}
old: Small good deeds do not really count.
new: Any good deed could be the one that makes my scale heavy.
try: Do three tiny good deeds today and do not tell anyone.

title: Light scales mean losing your own self.
subtitle: The worst loss is the loss of the soul
then: Ibn Kathir says this is {trap}when evil deeds outweigh good deeds{/trap}; they are doomed and {trap}have ended up with the worst deal{/trap}. Not a lost fortune but {trap}a lost self.{/trap}
now: You panic over a lost wallet, a failed investment, a broken phone screen. {idea}Those losses can be replaced. This verse names the one loss that cannot.{/idea} And today you can still add to the other side.
old: The worst thing that could happen is losing what I have.
new: The worst loss is losing myself, and I can work against it today.
try: Ask Allah tonight to make your scale heavy, and do one good deed to start.

title: The Fire meets the faces that turned away.
subtitle: A sober warning, told to protect you

row.title: to turn you while you can

then: Ibn Kathir links this to verses saying {trap}fire will cover their faces{/trap} and they will not be able to ward it off. Ibn Abbas explained their look as {trap}frowning{/trap}. It describes the end of those whose scales were light.
now: Your face turned toward the screen at prayer time. Your face turned away from the person asking for help. {idea}The warning is about your face, and today you choose where it turns.{/idea}
old: Warnings about Hell are only meant to scare people.
new: The warning is a mercy telling me to turn my face toward Allah now.
try: At your next prayer, place your forehead down slowly and ask Allah to protect your face from the Fire.

title: Were My verses not recited to you?
subtitle: No excuse left after the message came
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah tells them: {idea}I sent Messengers, revealed Books, and cleared the confusion, so you have no excuse.{/idea} He cites: We never punish until We have sent a Messenger.
now: You have a Quran app on your phone. Translations in your language. Lectures for free. {idea}The verse you are reading right now has been recited to you.{/idea}
old: I did not know enough to be responsible.
new: The message has reached me, and that is both a gift and a responsibility.
try: Read the meaning of one more verse today, slowly, as if it was sent to you.

title: Our wretchedness overcame us, they will say.
subtitle: A confession that comes too late
then: Ibn Kathir explains: {trap}evidence was established against us, but we were so doomed we could not follow it, so we went astray.{/trap} They admit everything, but only after the door has closed.
now: You know the habit that keeps beating you. You could say it to Allah today: {idea}my Lord, my weakness wins sometimes, help me.{/idea} The same confession, said now, is the start of change.
old: I will admit my faults when I have to.
new: Confessing my faults to Allah today is a mercy, not a defeat.
try: Tell Allah honestly today one weakness that keeps beating you, and ask for help.

title: Take us out, and if we return, we are wrongdoers.
subtitle: A promise made from the wrong side of the door
then: They will ask: {trap}our Lord, bring us out, and if we go back to what we did, we will be wrongdoers.{/trap} Ibn Kathir links it to another verse: {trap}is there any way to get out?{/trap} There is none, because they associated partners while the believers worshipped Him alone.
now: After the hangover, the fight, the lost money, you swear: never again. {idea}You get to make that promise now, in this world, where it can still be kept.{/idea}
old: I will change once things get bad enough.
new: The time to promise and keep it is now, while I still have the world.
try: Make one sincere "never again" today about a habit, and take one step to keep it.

title: Stay in it, despised, and do not speak to Me.
subtitle: The door of asking finally closes
then: Ibn Kathir says it means {trap}do not ask for this again, for I will not respond{/trap}. Ibn Abbas said these are the words of Ar-Rahman when silencing them. It is the most sober moment in the surah: {trap}asking itself is no longer accepted.{/trap}
