now: Today Allah says: call on Me, I will answer. {reward}You can speak to Him at 3 a.m., in traffic, in a whisper.{/reward} The verse shows what it means to lose that, so you treasure it now.
old: I can always talk to Allah later.
new: Being allowed to speak to Allah is a gift I should use every day.
try: Talk to Allah for five minutes today in your own words, about anything.

title: A group of My servants said: forgive us, have mercy.
subtitle: The dua of the ones who were mocked
then: Allah reminds the people of the Fire of {idea}a party of My servants{/idea} who used to pray: {reward}our Lord, we believe, so forgive us and have mercy on us, You are the best of the merciful.{/reward} Ibn Kathir calls them His believing servants and close friends.
now: Your coworker who steps out to pray. Your quiet aunt who whispers dua all through the family dinner. {idea}Allah calls such people "My servants".{/idea} You can be one of them with one sincere sentence.
old: Only very pious people are Allah's special servants.
new: Those who humbly ask for forgiveness are the ones Allah calls His own.
try: Memorize this dua today: Rabbana amanna faghfir lana warhamna wa anta khayrur-rahimin.

title: You mocked them until it made you forget Me.
subtitle: How ridicule hardens the mocker
then: Ibn Kathir says {trap}you made fun of them for calling on Me and praying to Me{/trap}, and {trap}your hatred for them made you forget what I would do to you{/trap}. He cites: the criminals used to laugh at the believers and wink at each other.
now: The group chat sends a meme about the "too religious" friend. Everyone laughs, including you. {trap}Mocking someone's worship slowly dulls your own.{/trap}
old: It is just a joke; it does not hurt anyone.
new: Mocking someone's sincerity can make me forget Allah myself.
try: If anyone jokes about someone's worship today, do not join. Change the subject kindly.

title: Their patience was rewarded; they are the winners.
subtitle: The mocked become the successful
then: Ibn Kathir explains: {reward}for the harm and mockery you inflicted on them, I have caused them to attain the victory of joy, safety, Paradise and salvation from the Fire.{/reward} {idea}Patience was what turned the mockery into reward.{/idea}
now: You wear your hijab to a new job and catch the looks. You leave the party early to pray and hear the comments. {idea}Every bit of patience is being written down.{/idea}
old: Putting up with ridicule for my faith is a loss.
new: Patience with mockery is exactly what Allah rewards.
try: The next time someone teases your faith, answer calmly, then say alhamdulillah to yourself.

title: How many years did you stay on earth?
subtitle: A question about the length of a life
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah {idea}tells them how much they wasted in their short lives by failing to obey Him{/idea}. If they had been patient during their short stay, {reward}they would have won like His pious friends{/reward}.
now: Your phone tells you your screen time each week. Imagine one screen that showed your whole life: {idea}how many hours went where?{/idea}
old: I have decades ahead of me.
new: One day I will be asked how long I stayed, so I count my years well.
try: Check your screen time today and give one hour back to something that matters.

title: A day or part of a day, they will say.
subtitle: A whole life shrinks to an afternoon

row.title: it will feel like a day

then: They will reply: {trap}we stayed a day or part of a day; ask those who keep count.{/trap} Ibn Kathir says this means {idea}those who keep the records{/idea}. Looking back, a whole lifetime will feel that short.
now: Your school days, your wedding, the birth of your first child. They already feel like yesterday. {idea}That is the feeling this verse describes, stretched over a whole life.{/idea}
old: Life is long, there is time to waste.
new: My whole life will feel like part of a day, so I fill today well.
try: Tonight, look back at today and name one hour you would spend differently tomorrow.

title: You stayed only a little, if only you had known.
subtitle: Trading the eternal for the brief
then: Ibn Kathir says: {trap}it was only a short time, however you look at it.{/trap} If you had known, {idea}you would not have preferred the transient to the eternal{/idea}. If you had obeyed patiently like the believers, {reward}you would have won as they did{/reward}.
now: Five minutes of anger that cost a friendship. One night of fun that cost a marriage. {idea}The short thing always looks bigger up close.{/idea} You know now, so you can choose differently.
old: What I want now matters more than what comes later.
new: This life is a little while, so I will not trade forever for it.
try: Before one tempting choice today, ask: will this matter in a hundred years?

title: Did you think We created you for nothing?
subtitle: Your life has a purpose and a return
then: Ibn Kathir explains: {trap}did you think you were created in vain, with nothing required of you?{/trap} Or created to play and amuse yourselves like animals with no reward or punishment? {idea}But you were created to worship Allah and carry out His commands.{/idea}
now: A Sunday spent on the sofa, scrolling, with a dull feeling that nothing you do matters. {idea}This verse says the opposite: your life was made on purpose, and you are going back to the One who made it.{/idea}
old: Life is random and I am just passing time.
new: I was created on purpose, and I am going back to Allah.
try: Write one line today answering: what am I living for? Keep it where you will see it.

title: Exalted is Allah, the True King, Lord of the Noble Throne.
subtitle: Far above creating anything in vain
then: Ibn Kathir says He is {idea}sanctified above the idea that He should create anything in vain, for He is the True King{/idea}. The Throne is mentioned as {reward}the highest point of creation, described as karim: beautiful in appearance and splendid in form{/reward}.
now: Earthly kings and bosses make random decisions and change their minds. {idea}The True King never does anything without wisdom, including making you.{/idea}
old: Some of what happens in my life is pointless.
new: The True King does nothing in vain, including what He does with me.
try: Think of one hardship you thought was pointless. Ask Allah to show you its wisdom.

title: Calling on another god has no proof, and cannot succeed.
subtitle: The surah's final word on success
then: Ibn Kathir says whoever worships anything with Allah has {trap}no evidence for what he says{/trap}, and {idea}Allah will call him to account{/idea}. They will not prosper or be saved. The surah opened with {reward}the believers have succeeded{/reward} and closes on its mirror.
now: You lean on the lucky charm, the horoscope, the person you think can fix everything. {trap}Ask what proof you have that any of it can help.{/trap} {idea}The surah began and ends with one question: what is real success?{/idea}
old: It does not hurt to rely on other things alongside Allah.
new: Only reliance on Allah has proof behind it, and only it leads to success.
try: Remove one thing from your life you rely on without any real basis.

title: The surah closes with a plea for forgiveness and mercy.
subtitle: The surah ends by handing you a dua

row.title: have mercy
sub: guide me to say and do good

then: After all the warnings, Allah teaches the Prophet ﷺ and us one last line. Ibn Kathir says {idea}forgiveness means wiping away sins and concealing them from people{/idea}, and {reward}mercy means guiding a person and helping him say and do good things{/reward}.
now: You finish a long surah full of warnings, and maybe you feel heavy. {reward}Allah does not leave you there. He gives you the words to ask Him: forgive me, have mercy on me.{/reward}
old: After reading all those warnings, I feel there is no hope for me.
new: The surah ends by teaching me to ask the Best of the merciful, so hope is open.
try: Say this dua today, slowly, three times: Rabbighfir warham wa anta khayrur-rahimin.
